text:
Mine Drainage - Any water accumulating in open pits will be pumped to an internal drainage system.
In addition, any dilute waters from direct precipitation or snowmelt which the internal drainage system can collect (e.g., via small collection ponds, runoff from undisturbed areas, etc.) would aid in the dilution of mine drainage water collected throughout the mine area.
pH data for most overburden samples are within allowable limits (6.0 - 9.0), however in the event that alkaline mine drainage problems are so severe that the water from the interior drainage system cannot be released to natural surface drainage, a facility for chemical treatment to neutralize alkaline mine drainage water will be provided. Although neutralization will decrease pH and reduce alkalinity, the resulting water may still contain high levels of sulfates and dissolved solids. Water from internal drainage will not be released to the natural drainage system unless it meets current water-quality standards of the Montana Pollution Discharge Elimination System and the Montana Mining and Reclamation Law. Dilution of alkaline mine drainage water appears to be one of the best treatments for mitigating its impact.
Dust Control - Water distributed on roads of the mining area for dust control should be relatively low in dissolved solids content. Currently well water from the Madison formation receives primary treatment to decrease dissolved solids prior to being utilized for dust control.

Biocides - The application of pesticides and herbicides in and around the mining areas of Tract II and III is highly unlikely (David W. Simpson, personal comm.). If their use is found to be necessary and if the compounds used are of a persistant nature, water quality monitoring studies will be appropriately modified.
